First, we substitute $u=3y-2.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}y}=3\,⟹\,\text{d}u=3\text{d}y.
$$

Since $u\to -\infty $ when $y\to -\infty ,$ the table for the limits of integration using the rule $u=3y-2$ is as follows:

| $y$ | $-\infty $ | $0$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $-\infty $ | $-2$ |

So, the integral in terms of the new variable $u$ is

$$
{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{8}{(3y-2)^{6}}\,\text{d}y={\int }_{-\infty }^{-2}\frac{8}{3{u}^{6}}\,\text{d}u
$$

Finally, we proceed by setting the lower bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to -\infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{-2}\frac{8}{3{u}^{6}}\,\text{d}u & =\frac{8}{3}{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{-2}{u}^{-6}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{8}{3}{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[-\frac{1}{5}{u}^{-5}]}_{a}^{-2} \\  & =-\frac{8}{15}\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[\frac{1}{{u}^{5}}]}_{a}^{-2} \\  & =-\frac{8}{15}\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }[\frac{1}{(-2)^{5}}-\frac{1}{{a}^{5}}] \\  & =-\frac{8}{15}\cdot (-\frac{1}{32}-0) \\  & =\frac{1}{60}.\end{aligned}
$$
